body: This definitely needs some steps to reproduce it reliably

I was able to narrow this down to having _any_ gdextension added to the project. Here's an example with a blank project that has the godot-git-plugin installed.

[import-crash-test.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22924527/import-crash-test.tar.gz)

Trigger the crash with `rm -rf .godot; godot --headless --import`
Workaround for anyone hitting this: use `xvfb-run godot ...` instead of `--headless`

I also ran into this when exporting a Godot project which uses a godot-rust extension. Here is a simple nix-based reproducer: https://github.com/MichaelMMacLeod/godot-crash-export/. It can be run with:
```sh
nix build github:MichaelMMacLeod/godot-crash-export
```

Minimal-ish reproducer:
- Clone https://github.com/akien-mga/threen/
- `git submodule update --init`
- Delete `doc_classes/Threen.xml` - the bug is specific to GDExtension _without_ documentation
- `scons`
- Copy `bin` to `demo/bin`
- Import the demo with `godot --headless --import`
- When repeating tests, make sure to delete the `.godot` folder

CC @deralmas @RandomShaper 

Seems to be a race condition on cleanup, where `EditorHelp::cleanup_doc()` deletes `doc` when the main thread still has a deferred call to `_gen_extensions_docs` to handle.

@akien-mga > the bug is specific to GDExtension without documentation I tried adding documentation to the class in the extension in my reproducer but still managed to reproduce the crash: https://github.com/MichaelMMacLeod/godot-crash-export/commit/8ebaaa531c9dbb581f7c4e3513d834842d008b18 Maybe there's some difference in how docs are generated on the C++ side vs the Rust side?

Reproducible on macOS with 4.6.3-stable official (arm64, editor build). A project containing the spine-godot GDExtension (spine-runtimes 4.3.0) plus a single skeleton asset crashes on exit from `--headless --import` **every time** when the import cache is cold (no `.godot/`, no `*.import` files). With a warm cache the same command exits cleanly, which fits the deferred-docs explanation: the docs already exist, so nothing gets queued.

```
rm -rf .godot && find assets -name "*.import" -delete
Godot --headless --import .   # exit 134
```

Backtrace from 4.6.3-stable official:

```
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11
```

A version datapoint that may help narrow the regression: the same project with the same extension binary imports cleanly on **4.4.1-stable** (3/3 runs, official and a custom editor build), while 4.6-based builds crash 100% for me (4.6.3 official 3/3, plus two custom editor builds of 4.6/4.6.3 at 8/8 and 3/3). #111048 lists 4.5.beta4 as the oldest reproducible version, so with 4.4.1 clean the regression lands somewhere in the 4.5 dev cycle.

Can also confirm the `--frame-delay 800` workaround from #111048: with it the cold import exits 0 (2/2). A note for anyone hitting this in CI: the import itself completes before the crash, the `.import` artifacts and `.godot/` cache are written, only the exit code is garbage. So a retry (now warm) or `--frame-delay` unblocks pipelines.

macOS 14.7.4 (23H420), Apple M3 Pro.
